SddFeature.keywords: feature, small-change, brownfield, scope-freeze, narrow-recon, short-interview, spec-delta, red-green, diff-review, sdd-feature
SddFeature.Mission:
Add or change a bounded piece of behaviour in EXISTING code, end to end, in one session: confirm size and boundary → exact reading of the touch point → short interview → small spec delta approved once → red tests → green code → one diff review → report.
This is the default route for ordinary product work in a brownfield project: a product feature, a new API method, a handler, a flag, a field. The flow has one operator approval (the spec delta) and one reviewer (the final diff). Tickets, scaffold, approval #2, the spec review cycle and audit belong to the full flow and stay there.
The change reuses the existing architecture. A change that needs a new scope, module, public entity, cross-scope contract, external dependency, or an architecture choice leaves through `H_TOO_BIG` to the full flow.
The root session does the work itself. Subagents: one read-only reviewer at `STEP_6_CHECK`, plus a read-only search agent when the touch point spans many files.
Input — operator intent: what to add or change, constraints, what stays untouched. Output — spec delta, tests and code in the working tree, uncommitted; a report listing the agent's own decisions and a «На потом» list.
SddFeature.BeliefState:
Inherited from the loading directive (already in context): AX_NO_PROCESS_NARRATION, AX_OPERATOR_DIALOGUE_STYLE, AX_OPERATOR_LANGUAGE, AX_OPERATOR_OUTPUT_LIVE_TEXT, AX_TOOL_INVOCATION, HALT_FORMAT
Orchestrator holds full project context — the ONLY actor able to detect duplication against existing code/specs (the isolated critic cannot). For every entity/type/method/contract the artifact introduces, reconcile before accepting it: REUSE existing (adapt artifact to it) > EXTEND existing > JUSTIFY new (record one-line rationale in artifact: why existing surface is insufficient) > ESCALATE to operator. Unjustified new surface is a finding to resolve, not to wave through. Bias toward consolidation — do not let the system grow a duplicate entity each round.
The operator confirms the size before any design question. A size trigger is any of: a new scope or module; a new public entity in a spec inventory; an architecture alternative that must be chosen; a change to a contract another scope consumes; a new external dependency; a spec delta beyond about 60 lines or three spec files; an expected diff beyond about 15 code files. A trigger found at any step is reported as it is, with its evidence; the operator may still answer «делаем здесь», and that answer is recorded in the report.
The boundary is fixed before the first question: a «Не делаем» list built from the operator's own words plus the obvious neighbours (other entry points, renames, old debts), confirmed together with the size. After that the boundary moves only by the operator's explicit words. An answer to a question, a reference project, or a gap the agent noticed leaves the boundary where it is; whatever turns up outside goes to «На потом».
Recon is narrow in breadth and exact in depth. The touch point is read to the line: the code that will change, its direct callers and wiring (flags, construction, mount points), every spec section that mentions the touched behaviour, and the tests around it. The real gaps of a reuse are found only by exact reading. The rest of the scope, sibling features and reference projects stay unread unless the operator asks.
A hole is triaged before it is asked: - **Блокирует** — the change cannot work or cannot be specified without an answer that code and specs do not contain → a question, with the SMALLEST working option recommended first. - **По умолчанию** — a defensible, cheap-to-change default exists → take it and list it under «Принял без вопроса». - **На потом** — real but outside the boundary → one line in «На потом». Budget: five questions for the whole flow, in at most two `AskUserQuestion` calls. A sixth question is a size trigger per `AX_SIZE_CONFIRMED`. A solution the operator already named is settled: confirm it fits and ask only where it breaks. A reference the operator points at answers only the question it was given; its other differences are at most three one-liners in «На потом». A counter-question gets a plain answer and one return to the original question carrying only what changed.
The agreed result of the interview is a spec DELTA, written before any code and approved once; the operator signs the delta, and the chat is only how it was reached. The delta holds the new or changed requirement lines edited in place, the scenarios for the new behaviour (including the flag-off or fallback scenario when a flag is involved), and a Decision Log entry only for a non-obvious trade-off. A confirmed default, a refusal, or a clarification is conversation and stays out of the Decision Log. The delta is a surgical `Edit` of the owning spec: neighbouring sections and unrelated spec debt keep their bytes, and debt met on the way is listed in «На потом».
Every scenario of the delta maps to a test at the cheapest level that can prove it. The tests are written first, run, and seen failing for the right reason — the behaviour is absent. Then comes the minimal code that makes them pass.
The verification tail is the agent's own diff-against-delta sweep plus ONE fresh read-only reviewer over the diff. The reviewer returns `CLEAN` or at most five evidence-backed findings and judges only lines the diff changed; older debt it meets is listed separately and blocks nothing. A finding the agent confirms against the code is fixed in one pass. A second look happens only when a fix changed behaviour, and it is a narrowed recheck of exactly those fixes. A finding that needs a behaviour choice goes to the operator as a question.
A decision the agent made alone while implementing (an unlisted default, a helper it had to add, a scenario it could not automate, an old defect it worked around) is noted as it happens and shown to the operator once, in the report, with the choices «принять как есть · переделать · откатить». Implementation continues without stopping for it.
SddFeature.HaltConditions: | ID | Trigger | |---|---| | `H_TOO_BIG` | A size trigger of `AX_SIZE_CONFIRMED` fired — name it, offer the full flow; continue here only on the operator's explicit «делаем здесь» | | `H_NOT_A_FEATURE` | The request is a defect: observed behaviour differs from intended and nothing new is designed — hand to the fix flow | | `H_NO_OWNING_SPEC` | No spec owns the touched behaviour and the operator declined a thin spec for it | | `H_DELTA_REJECTED` | The operator rejected the delta twice — ask what the target behaviour is | | `H_RED_NOT_RED` | A new test passes before any code change, or fails for a reason other than the missing behaviour |

Step.Goal: One confirmation: what is done, what is left out, and that it is small.
Step.Action:
Consume `routerState` from the entry skill; do not repeat `sdd-state`. Restate the request in at most three lines, per `AX_OPERATOR_DIALOGUE_STYLE` and `AX_OPERATOR_OUTPUT_LIVE_TEXT`, without narrating routing per `AX_NO_PROCESS_NARRATION`. Draft «Не делаем» per `AX_SCOPE_FREEZE` and check the triggers of `AX_SIZE_CONFIRMED`. A defect → `H_NOT_A_FEATURE`. A trigger → `H_TOO_BIG`.
Ask ONE `AskUserQuestion`: «Делаю как доработку: <одна строка>. Не трогаю: <список>. Верно?» with options «Да (рекомендую)» · «Поправить границы» · «Это крупнее — полный флоу». This is the size confirmation the router skipped for this route; design questions wait for `STEP_2_SHORT_INTERVIEW`.

Step.Goal: Know exactly how the touch point works today and where the request does not fit.
Step.Action:
Per `AX_NARROW_NOT_SHALLOW`, read the code to change with its callers and wiring, the spec sections that mention the behaviour, and the neighbouring tests. Find the owning spec through the code file header (`@spec`) and the specs portal. Produce three short working lists: **Берём готовым** (reused as is, per `AX_REUSE_FIRST`), **Дыры** (where the request as stated would not work or contradicts a spec, each with `file:line`), **Что говорит спека** (the sections that will change and any that already promise this behaviour).
A spec that contradicts the request is a «Блокирует» question. A size trigger found here → `H_TOO_BIG`.
When no spec owns the touched code — the normal state of legacy code — the delta goes into a thin spec that covers this behaviour only: propose its path in the `STEP_3_SPEC_DELTA` card. Recovering the whole module's spec from code is separate work and goes to «На потом». The operator declining a thin spec → `H_NO_OWNING_SPEC`.

Step.Goal: Close the blocking holes and nothing else.
Step.Action:
Triage every hole per `AX_ASK_ONLY_BLOCKERS`. With no blocking hole, go to `STEP_3_SPEC_DELTA` with zero questions.
Otherwise send one message: two lines of what was found (reuse confirmed, N holes), then the questions — each one sentence of situation, the smallest working option first, the alternative, one line of consequence — batched in one `AskUserQuestion`. A second call is used only when an answer opened a new blocking hole. Under the questions list «Принял без вопроса» (one line each, the operator corrects by number) and «На потом» so far. The boundary of `AX_SCOPE_FREEZE` holds through every answer.

Step.Goal: The agreed behaviour is written down and approved once.
Step.Action:
Write the delta into the owning spec per `AX_DELTA_BEFORE_CODE`, as a surgical `Edit`. Keep it readable per `AX_READER_WITHOUT_SESSION_CONTEXT`: the delta names behaviour, not this conversation. For an existing V2 spec, check its structure: npx gennady sdd-check --spec --authoring Inputs : exact path of the spec edited in this step. Use deltaReceipt. Fix only findings on the lines this step wrote; findings on older lines go to «На потом».
Show ONE approval card: the scenarios (title plus one line each), the changed requirement lines, the test plan (scenario → level → test file), the files expected to change, «Не делаем», «На потом». Each item states its meaning in plain words with its ID in parentheses. Then `AskUserQuestion`: «Утверждаете?» — «Да, пишу тесты и код (рекомендую)» · «Есть правки». On «Есть правки» apply them, show only the changed lines, ask again; a second rejection → `H_DELTA_REJECTED`.
This approval is approval #1 for the edited spec. Record it in that spec's approval marker with `Reviewed set` naming that spec and `Independent review: pending`; `STEP_6_CHECK` updates the review field. Other specs keep their markers. No task index and no approval #2 marker is written in this flow.

Step.Goal: Failing tests that state the new behaviour.
Step.Action: Per `AX_RED_BEFORE_GREEN`, write the tests of the plan with names that mirror the scenario titles, using the test level and commands the project already uses for the touched area. Run them and confirm each fails because the behaviour is absent; otherwise `H_RED_NOT_RED` — repair the test before any production code.

Step.Goal: Minimal code that makes them pass.
Step.Action: Implement with reuse first per `AX_REUSE_FIRST`. A new or touched code file carries the project's file header pointing at the owning spec; this flow has no Task-ID, so none is written. Run the targeted tests until green, then the project's own gates for the touched area (its test and lint commands as the repository defines them). Note every own decision for `AX_DEVIATIONS_AT_END` as it is made.

Step.Goal: The diff does what the delta says — no less, no more.
Step.Action:
Own sweep first: for each scenario of the delta — the test that exercises it and the code that implements it; for each changed code path — the scenario that asked for it. Code without a scenario is a deviation or is removed; a scenario without a test is a gap to close.
Then, per `AX_ONE_REVIEW_NO_LOOP`, dispatch ONE fresh read-only reviewer with the `git diff` (spec delta, tests, code), the paths of the owning specs, and these questions: does the code implement each scenario and the fallback path; does any test assert code shape instead of the outcome; does the diff contradict another statement of the owning spec; is anything in the diff inside «Не делаем»; does a new entity duplicate an existing one. It returns `CLEAN` or at most five findings with `file:line` evidence, never edits, and is not retained.
Verify each finding against the code: real → fix in one pass and re-run the affected tests; not real → reject with the line that resolves it; needs a behaviour choice → an operator question in `STEP_7_REPORT`. Set the marker's review field to `clean` or `findings resolved`.

Step.Goal: The operator knows what is true now and what is theirs to decide.
Step.Action: Send one message per `FEATURE_REPORT_FORMAT`. When own decisions or open behaviour choices exist, follow it with ONE `AskUserQuestion` over them per `AX_DEVIATIONS_AT_END` and apply the answers. The flow ends at the report: commit, push and merge request wait for the operator's word, and the full-flow menu (critic, scaffold, audit) is not offered.

Contracts.Contract:
``` ✅ <что теперь умеет продукт — одна строка>
**Что сделано** - Спека: <файл> — , <что изменено> - Тесты: <файлы> — , были красными по причине <…>, теперь зелёные - Код: , +/−; переиспользовано: <…>
**Проверки** - <команда> → <результат> (каждая запущенная; незапущенные — отдельной строкой с причиной) - Ревью диффа:
**Решил сам** (если есть) 1. <что> — <почему> — <где>
**На потом** (если есть) - <что> — <где видно>
Ничего не закоммичено. ```
